limitations: Only three of four fixed source strata yielded literal question headings; visual inspection of all seven EPA PDF pages confirmed declarative headings, not eligible questions.
Three covered questions are below the predeclared twelve-covered floor; nine genuine administrative controls exceed the six-outside floor.
Agency FAQs are a curated topical sample, not everyday visitor demand or reader comprehension.

The BLS FAQ was already a cited, previously checked authoring source; independent prior question non-exposure is not established. Native provenance remains development rather than claiming a sealed fresh candidate.
All wording and body labels precede retrieval predictions, but temporal freezing alone does not certify independence or representativeness.
Prepared CPI and electricity-unit reviews return public HTTP 404; source-published status is not actual publication.

The live consensus review differs from source uncertainty wording; the complete live body was inspected and its unchanged agreement conclusion supports the preassigned destination. No production text was changed.

rows.bodyGradingReason: The reviews explain long-term climate patterns and attribution, but neither gives a complete general definition spanning the scope of climate change. The attribution guide is adjacent context, not a complete terminology answer.

The attribution review establishes global warming and its cause, not the explicit distinction between temperature rise and the broader set of climate changes. A shared climate keyword is not sufficient.

The complete bottom line and stable-core paragraphs directly distinguish local, short-term weather from long-term statistical climate patterns and explain why isolated cold events do not measure a global climate trend.

The tree-planting review explains why emissions reductions still matter and why one mitigation tool is insufficient. It does not answer which future changes can still be prevented, the relevant time horizons or the meaning of too late.

The entire consensus review answers the core expert-agreement question with assessments, literature studies and limitations on exact agreement percentages. It distinguishes public controversy from expert disagreement.
As phrased this asks for an agency's institutional role, not an evidence-backed claim about a climate outcome. A NASA citation in a review does not supply an organizational-role answer.

These complete reviews identify several independent land, ocean, atmosphere and ice indicators, but do not provide a general taxonomy of climate observations and proxy records. Source-linked information is not automatically included in the reviewed body.

The body describes controls and homogenization, but not the complete global temperature construction, spatial aggregation and anomaly procedure. An urban-bias explanation alone is not the full measurement answer.

The full bottom line and stable core directly establish that raw station records need quality controls, adjustments and homogenization for station moves, instruments and urbanization. The misconception discussion explains why a thermometer can require correction without invalidating the global record.

The body establishes adjustment and homogenization needs, but does not explicitly distinguish invalid-record elimination from the later processing stages or explain the complete sequence as the question requests.

Station moves and neighboring-record comparisons are relevant climate examples, not a complete explanation of changing data provenance in general. The original question lacks a climate qualifier; no source-context words were added to make retrieval easier.

Independent datasets and neighboring records provide a relevant validation example, but the broad question asks how data-processing reliability is established generally. The query's missing climate qualifier remains unaltered.

The prepared review defines population-average price change and weights, but is not a complete CPI introduction. It is not promoted to a complete answer, and its source-published label must not substitute for actual public availability.

The source says defined population without supplying the CPI-U/CPI-W population definitions required to answer whose buying habits are represented. This is a missing named-population explanation, not an outside control.

Prepared reviews explain why CPI is not an individual's complete cost-of-living certificate and separate shelter services from asset purchases. They do not fully explain the CPI's relation to a conceptual cost-of-living index.
The source does not identify the particular headline CPI series reported by media. An index-reference explanation is not an answer about the named series; the missing distinction remains a gap.
This asks for agency release/subscription logistics, not a reviewed scientific or measurement claim. It is retained as an administrative outside control.
This asks where to obtain additional agency information or contact support. It is an administrative resource-navigation request, not an evidence conclusion.

The actual market-basket determination and expenditure-survey pipeline are missing. Prepared toy weighting examples explicitly disclaim BLS's real estimator and cannot answer this production-method question.
The actual CPI sampling procedure is missing. General statements about a defined basket, population or source scope do not explain the sample design.
The prepared numerical examples expressly are not the complete BLS production formula. They cannot be used to claim coverage of how the actual CPI is calculated.

The prepared body explains revisions to seasonal factors and data vintage, but not the complete distinction among corrected errors, adjusted revisions and unadjusted series policy. Its limited processing explanation remains partial.

In its fixed CPI-FAQ context this is a request for the agency's publication offerings, not evidence about a measured phenomenon. The unqualified original wording is preserved rather than expanded for retrieval.
This asks for the agency's area-index availability and publication schedule. No current schedule is inferred from statistical-definition reviews.
The question asks whether an agency supplies a particular download/data service. It does not ask for the production amounts themselves and is retained as an administrative availability control.
This asks about the agency's forecasting-service coverage at state level, not a particular forecast's scientific accuracy. No forecast or named state result is invented.
The question concerns whether the agency publishes a price series, not the price value or an energy outcome. It is a series-availability control.

No inspected canonical review provides the short-ton/metric-ton conversion. The site already covers physical measurement definitions, so this missing unit explanation is not reclassified outside merely to improve the denominator.
This requires dated U.S. coal-reserve inventory, definition and uncertainty. A review about coal-related emissions or diamond origins cannot answer that named quantitative question.
This requires a dated U.S. generating-plant count and counting convention. Generic grid or power-plant technology discussions do not supply it.
This requires dated export quantities and destination countries, absent from the reviewed bodies. A climate conclusion about coal is not a trade-inventory answer.
This requires dated import quantities and origin countries. The missing named-context quantities remain a gap rather than an outside control.

The electricity-unit and lifecycle reviews do not provide fuel quantities per generated kWh with heat content and plant-efficiency assumptions for all three requested fuels. Lifecycle CO2e/kWh is a different quantity.

The SMR review discusses prospective cost limitations, not comparable generation costs across power-plant types, dates and accounting boundaries. The electricity guides do not supply the missing comparison.

The lifecycle review reports technology emission-intensity estimates, not the share of dated U.S. CO2 emissions associated with generation. Emission intensity and inventory share must not be substituted.
This is a catalog/definition request about the agency's price-series offerings, not a substantive coal-price value or causal energy claim. It is retained as a publication-metadata control.
